mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 5.0% (as of the most recent month) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the win rate (proportion of 20-day periods with positive returns) is below 60% when FEDFUNDS < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals worsening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the last two months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 1% in 2 months, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < INDPRO(t-1)) and unemployment above 4.0% (UNRATE > 4.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward 20-day returns due to reduced corporate output and weak consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines from previous month and UNRATE > 4.0%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines and UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 3.0% (yoy) indicates persistent inflation, which typically triggers a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL yoy inflation > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly growth rate in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0%) and a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) signals stagflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL yoy inflation > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level below 1200 thousand units indicates a weakening housing market, which reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 1200, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
